rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent single mass with a bent/stepped upper body and a carved lower frontage, so it clears the basic parcel/continuity gates. In plan and section it shows a believable dominant gesture, but the access response is only moderate: the blue frontage is acknowledged by a recess/undercut rather than a strongly legible public threshold, and the void is somewhat constrained relative to the solid. The form is not just a generic box, and it resonates well with the supplied neighborhood-architecture references, especially in the courtyard/bridge/terrace family. Program fit is acceptable for neighborhood living because the mass can plausibly hold compact mixed-use residential/commercial-like ground relationship, but the section is still closer to an abstract carved block than a fully resolved active street building. The geometry graph appears internally consistent and the protected cantilever ancestry is intact; no obvious cross-view collisions are visible.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a large carved central void and an upper bridge-like connector; good precedent for active courtyard/public-threshold organization.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/podium in scale than compact neighborhood street building.
